title: Podman creates a healthcheck timer even when HEALTHCHECK NONE is passed in the Containerfile
body:
Podman creates a healthcheck timer even when HEALTHCHECK NONE is passed in the Containerfile.

The container reports `Test: ["NONE"]`, but a systemd timer and service are created on start and recreated on restart. **Expected:** `HEALTHCHECK NONE` should prevent regular healthcheck scheduling, regardless of retained interval defaults.

Reproduced with source-built **Podman 6.1.4**, rootless on Ubuntu 24.04 / WSL2, through both the native CLI and Docker-compatible API 1.44.

## Reproducer

Use Podman 6.1.4 with a working systemd user manager and `DISABLE_HC_SYSTEMD` unset. Comments show the relevant recorded output; container IDs are abbreviated and unit descriptions omitted.

```bash
workdir=$(mktemp -d)
image="localhost/podman-none-repro-$$"
container="podman-none-repro-$$"

cat > "$workdir/Containerfile" <<'EOF'
FROM docker.io/library/alpine:3.21
HEALTHCHECK NONE
EOF

podman build --format=docker -t "$image" "$workdir"

cid=$(podman create --name "$container" --network=none \
    "$image" /bin/sh -c 'while :; do sleep 1; done')

podman container init "$container"

podman start "$container"

podman inspect --format '{{json .Config.Healthcheck}}' "$container"
# {"Test":["NONE"],"Interval":30000000000,"Timeout":30000000000,"Retries":3}

systemctl --user list-units --all --plain --no-legend \
    "*$cid*.timer" "*$cid*.service"
# <cid>-1d928a614ee7ad72.service loaded inactive dead
# <cid>-1d928a614ee7ad72.timer   loaded active   elapsed

podman restart --time=0 "$container"

systemctl --user list-units --all --plain --no-legend \
    "*$cid*.timer" "*$cid*.service"
# <cid>-560def3262b437c0.service loaded inactive dead
# <cid>-560def3262b437c0.timer   loaded active   elapsed

# Cleanup only the resources created above.
podman rm --force --time=0 "$container"
podman rmi "$image"
rm -rf "$workdir"
```

## Cause

`disableHealthCheckSystemd()` checks the interval but does not use `HasHealthCheck()`, which already treats `NONE` as disabled. The inherited configuration retains a default 30-second interval, so it passes the timer gate.

The 6.1.4 reproduction reported:

```json

  "Test": [
    "NONE"
  ],
  "Interval": 30000000000,

  "Retries": 3
}
```

```text
b57456c2434ed6cc82dfd0e5b05fcf95bf3008b39a15e06d24f43e99eeeb20f0-1d928a614ee7ad72.timer   loaded active   elapsed /tmp/podman-6.1.4/podman --root /tmp/podman-none-reproducer/store --runroot /tmp/podman-none-reproducer/run --log-level warning --cgroup-manager cgroupfs --tmpdir /tmp/podman-none-reproducer/tmp --network-config-dir "" --volumepath /tmp/podman-none-reproducer/store/volumes --transient-store=false --hooks-dir /usr/share/containers/oci/hooks.d --runtime /tmp/podman-reproducer-runtime/crun-1.30.1-linux-amd64 --storage-driver vfs --events-backend file healthcheck run --ignore-result b57456c2434ed6cc82dfd0e5b05fcf95bf3008b39a15e06d24f43e99eeeb20f0
```

The same inherited-NONE failure was recorded through native Podman and Docker API 1.44. Both cases also created a timer after restart.

- Version: 6.1.4, source revision `464c15fec06f0074c916f9eff87c4806869c2833`; latest release when checked on 2026-10-15.
- Host: Ubuntu 24.04 / WSL2, amd64, kernel `6.18.54.1-microsoft-standard-WSL2`; Podman ran on the host, not inside a container.
- Runtime: crun 1.30.1, conmon 2.1.10.
- Private test store: `--storage-driver=vfs --cgroup-manager=cgroupfs --events-backend=file`.

The reproducer above is a shorter version of the recorded image/create/init/start/restart sequence and has not been separately rerun.

</details>
